solution: Solution: $y =\log_{\cot x}\tan x-\log_{\tan x}\cot x+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4x}{4-x^2}\right)$ $=\frac{\log_e\tan x}{\log_e\cot x}-\frac{\log_e\cot x}{\log_e\tan x}+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4x}{4-x^2}\right)$ $=\frac{\log_e\tan x}{\log_e\left(\frac{1}{\tan x}\right)}-\frac{\log_e\left(\frac{1}{\tan x}\right)}{\log_e(\tan x)}+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4x}{4-x^2}\right)$ $=\frac{\log_e\tan x}{-\log_e\tan x}+\frac{\log_e\tan x}{\log_e\tan x}+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4x}{4-x^2}\right)$ $=-1+1+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4x}{4-x^2}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4x}{4-x^2}\right)$ Now, $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{1+\left(\frac{4x}{4-x^2}\right)^2}\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{4x}{4-x^2}\right)$ $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{(4-x^2)^2}{(4-x^2)^2+16x^2}\left[\frac{(4-x^2)4+(4x)(2x)}{(4-x^2)^2}\right]$ $=\frac{(4-x^2)^2}{16+x^4+8x^2}\left[\frac{16-4x^2+8x^2}{(4-x^2)^2}\right]$ $=\frac{16+4x^2}{(x^2+4)^2}=\frac{4(x^2+4)}{(x^2+4)^2}$ $=\frac{4}{x^2+4}$ $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4}{4+x^2}$ © examsnet.com

solution: Solution: Given, $\int \cos(\log x) \,dx$ $= f(x)\{\cos(g(x))+\sin(h(x))\}$ $I=\int\limits_{II}\underset{I}{\cos(\log x)dx}$ { using by-part method of integration} $=\cos(\log x) \cdot x + \int \frac{\sin(\log x)}{x} \cdot x \,dx$ $=\cos(\log x) \cdot x + \int \sin(\log x) \,dx$ $=\cos(\log x) \cdot x$ $+\left[\sin(\log x) \cdot x - \int \frac{\cos(\log x)}{x} \cdot x \,dx\right]$ $I = x \cdot \cos(\log x) + x - \sin(\log x) - I$ $2I = x (\cos(\log x) + \sin(\log x))$ $\Rightarrow I = \frac{x}{2} (\cos(\log x) + \sin(\log x))$ $\therefore f(x)=\frac{x}{2} \Rightarrow f'(x)=\frac{1}{2}$ © examsnet.com

solution: Solution: $A=\{x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4}, x_{5}\}$ Mean $= \frac{\sum x_{i}}{5} = 2 \Rightarrow \sum\limits_{i=1}^{j} x_{i} = 10$ Variance, $\frac{1}{5-1} \left[ \sum x_{i}^{2} - \frac{\left(\sum x_{1}\right)^{2}}{5} \right] = 4$ $\Rightarrow \frac{1}{4} \left[ \sum x_{i}^{2} - \frac{(10)^{2}}{5} \right] = 4$ $\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}^{2} - 20 = 16$ $\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}^{2} = 36$ $B=\{y_{1}, y_{2}, y_{3} y_{4}, y_{5}\}$ , Mean $= \sum\limits_{i=1}^{5} \frac{y_{1}}{5} = 4$ $\Rightarrow \sum y_{i} = 20$ Variance, $\frac{1}{5-1} \left[ \sum y_{i}^{2} - \frac{\left(\sum y_{i}\right)^{2}}{5} \right] = 5$ $\Rightarrow \frac{1}{4} \left[ \sum y_{i}^{2} - \frac{(20)^{2}}{5} \right] = 5$ $\Rightarrow \sum y_{i}^{2} - 80 = 20$ $\Rightarrow \sum y_{i}^{2} = 100$ Now, $A \cup B = \{y_{1}, y_{2}, \dots, y_{5}, x_{1}, x_{2}, \dots, x_{5}\}$ , $= \{a_{i} ; i=1,2, \dots, 10\}$ $\text{Variance} = \frac{1}{10-1} \left[ \sum a_{i}^{2} - \frac{\left(\sum a_{i}\right)^{2}}{10} \right]$ $= \frac{1}{9} \left[ (x_{1}^{2}+x_{2}^{2}+\dots+x_{5}^{2}+y_{1}^{2}+\dots+y_{5}^{2}) - \frac{1}{10} \{ x_{1}+\dots+x_{5}+y_{1}+\dots+y_{5} \}^{2} \right]$ $= \frac{1}{9} \left[ \sum x_{i}^{2} + \sum y_{i}^{2} - \frac{1}{10} \{ \sum x_{i} + \sum y_{1} \}^{2} \right]$ $= \frac{1}{9} \left[ 36+100 - \frac{1}{10} (10+20)^{2} \right]$ $= \frac{46}{9} \sim 5.11$ © examsnet.com

question: Two integers are drawn at random from the set $\{5,6, \ldots, 35\}$ . What is the probability that their difference is odd?

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Two integers are drawn from $\{5,6, \ldots, 35\}$ Given, integer are 31 Total ways of choosing 2 integer from 31 integers $={}^{31}C_{2}$ Two integer difference will be odd only when one is even and other is odd. Let $A$ be the event of selecting two integers whose difference is odd. Now, $P(A)+P(\overline{A})=1$ $P(\overline{A})=$ Probability of selecting two integers whose difference is not odd. Case I When two integers are even. Total ways of choosing 2 integer (even) from 15 even integers $={}^{15}C_{2}$ Case II when two integers are odd Total ways $={}^{16}C_{2}$ $P(\overline{A})=\frac{{}^{15}C_{2}+{}^{16}C_{2}}{{}^{31}C_{2}}$ $=\frac{\frac{15\times14}{2}+\frac{16\times15}{2}}{\frac{31\times30}{2}}$ $P(\overline{A})=\frac{(15\times14)+(16\times15)}{31\times30}$ $=\frac{14+16}{31\times2}$ $=\frac{30}{2\times31}=\frac{15}{31}$ $\therefore P(A)=1-P(\overline{A})$ $=1-\frac{15}{31}$ $=\frac{31-15}{31}=\frac{16}{31}$ © examsnet.com

solution: Solution: Given, $3 P(X=4)=\frac{1}{2} P(X=4+P(X=0)$ $X$ is poisson distribution this gives $P(X=x)=\frac{e^{-\lambda} \lambda^{x}}{x!}$ $[x=0,1,2,\dots]$ Now, $3 P(X=4)=\frac{1}{2} P(X=2)+P(X=0)$ $\Rightarrow \frac{3 e^{-\lambda} \lambda^{4}}{4!} = \frac{1}{2} \frac{e^{-\lambda} \lambda^{2}}{2!} + \frac{e^{-\lambda} \lambda^{0}}{0!}$ $\Rightarrow \frac{3 \lambda^{4}}{4!} = \frac{\lambda^{2}}{4} + 1$ $\Rightarrow \frac{\lambda^{4}}{8} = \frac{\lambda^{2}}{4} + 1$ or $\lambda^{4} - 2 \lambda^{2} - 8 = 0$ Let $\lambda^{2} = u$ , then $u^{2} - 2u - 8 = 0$ Gives, $u = 4, -2$ $\therefore \lambda^{2} = 4$ $\Rightarrow \lambda = 2$ ∴ Mean of $X = 2$ © examsnet.com

question: Three Carnot engines operate in series between a heat source at temperature $T_{1}$ and heat sink at a temperature $T_{4}$ . There are two other reservoirs at temperatures $T_{2}$ and $T_{3}$ . The three engines are equally efficient if ______ (given that $T_{1}>T_{2}>T_{3}>T_{4})$

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Given, efficiencies $\eta_{1}=\eta_{2}=\eta_{3}=\eta$ and temperature, $T_{1}>T_{2}>T_{3}>T_{4}$ As we know that, in case of Carnot engine, Efficiency $(\eta)=1-\frac{T_{\mathrm{sink}}}{T_{\mathrm{source}}}$ $\therefore \eta_{1}=\eta=1-\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}$ $\Rightarrow T_{2}=( 1 -\eta) T_{1}$ ...(i) Similarly, $T_{3}=( 1 -\eta) T_{2}$ ...(ii) $T_{4}=( 1-\eta) T_{3}$ ...(iii) Now, by using Eqs. (i), (ii) and (iii), we get $(T_{1}^{2} \cdot T_{4})^{1/3} = \left[ \left( \frac{T_{2}}{1-\eta} \right)^{2} \cdot (1-\eta) T_{3} \right]^{1/3}$ $= \left[ \frac{T_{2}^{2}}{1-\eta} \cdot T_{3} \right]^{1/3}$ $= \left[ \left( \frac{T_{2}^{2}}{1-\eta} \right) (1-\eta) T_{2} \right]^{1/3}$ $= \left[ T_{2}^{3} \right]^{1/3}$ $= T_{2}$ Again, by using Eqs. (i), (ii) and (iii), we get $(T_{1} \cdot T_{3}^{2})^{1/3}$ $= \left[ \left( \frac{T_{2}}{1-\eta} \right) \left[ (1-\eta) T_{3} \right]^{2} \right]^{1/3}$ $= \left[ T_{2} (1-\eta) T_{3}^{2} \right]^{1/3}$ $= \left[ \frac{T_{3}}{1-\eta} (1-\eta) T_{3}^{2} \right]^{1/3}$ $= \left[ T_{3}^{3} \right]^{1/3} = T_{3}$ © examsnet.com

question: Identify the correct sequence with respect to the strength of hydrogen bonding among the following.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following statements are Correct? (i) Inductive effect $\&$ resonance effect is possible in chlorobenzene (ii) Resonance effect dominates orer inductive effect in Anisole (iii) P-nitrobenzoic acid is less acidic than $m$ -nitrobenzoic acid (iv) Diphenylamine is more basic than aniline

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: (i) The $\mathrm{Cl}$ group activates benzene ring more by resonance effect. $\mathrm{Cl}$ group being more electronegative withdraws electrons from benzene ring and shows - I effect. (ii) The methyl group of ether can donate electrons through inductive effect that is not as strong as electron donation effect to the pi-system. So, resonance effect dominates over inductive effect in anisole. (iii) $p$ -nitrobenzoic acid is more acidic than $m$ -nitrobenzoic acid. When both acids donate $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ from -COOH group, then $p$ -nitrobenzoate is more stabilised due to $m$ -effect of nitro group at meta position by deactivating the ring. So, statement (iii) is incorrect. (iv) Diphenylamine is less basic than aniline. The lone pair of $\mathrm{N}$ -atom in diphenylamine is delocalised on two benzene rings due to which it is less available to donate resulting into decrease in basicity. In aniline, it is delocalised on one benzene ring, so lone pair is more available for donation. Hence, it is more basic. So, statement IV is incorrect. © examsnet.com

question: Iron exhibits $BCC$ -structure at room temperature. Above $500^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , it transforms to $FCC$ -structure. Find the ratio of the density of iron at room temperature to that at $500^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . (Assume the atomic radii and the molar mass of iron remain constant even with variation in temperature)

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: We know, Density, $d=\frac{Z M}{a^{3} N_{0}}$ For bcc unit cell, $Z=2,\ a=\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} r$ $d_{\mathrm{bcc}}=\frac{2 M}{\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} r\right)^{3} N_{0}}$ For fcc unit cell, $Z=4,\ a=\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}} r$ $d_{\mathrm{fcc}}=\frac{4 M}{\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}} r\right)^{3} N_{0}}$ Ratio of density of iron bcc : fcc can be calculated by dividing Eq. (i) by Eq. (ii) $\frac{d_{\mathrm{fcc}}}{d_{\mathrm{fcc}}}=\frac{\frac{2 M}{\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} r\right)^{3} N_{0}}}{\frac{4 M}{\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}} r\right)^{3} N_{0}}}=\frac{1}{2}\times\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{3}$ $=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{3}{2}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4\sqrt{2}}$ The ratio is $3\sqrt{3}:4\sqrt{2}$ . © examsnet.com
